clue.text: Madder, say, when blushing

definitions.meaning: madder is a plant whose root yields a red dye, an example of a dye or tint
a blushing person is going red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone grows angrier while turning red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder is a classic dye, so a tint for fabric; and a person reddening with embarrassment is said to be doing this to the cheeks.

clue.text: Cards prepared to be chilly on ship's platform

parts.note: chilly means cold
a deck is the floor or platform of a ship

explanation.surface: A pack of cards is laid out on a cold ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: In card cheating, a stacked pack secretly swapped into the game is known by this name.

clue.text: Wake not recorded before noon

parts.note: a broadcast that is not recorded goes out live

explanation.surface: A funeral wake held before midday is not taped.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake up a party or a sleepy person is to rouse or enliven them.

clue.text: Dinner hours due to develop the ill-fed

indicators.note: to develop means to grow or change form, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Dinner hours are rescheduled to help the hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-fed lacks enough nutrition, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Integral part of the main Built Road

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the following words

explanation.surface: Built Road forms an essential section of the main thoroughfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is built into the whole as a fixed component.

clue.text: Marx, old grumbler originally

parts.note: a grouch is a grumbler or complainer

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so take the opening letter of the word old

explanation.surface: Karl Marx is cast as a grumpy old complainer from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Karl Marx; the definition is really one of the Marx Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Marx Brothers comedy team bore this stage name.

clue.text: Country's leader owned land in Africa

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so take the opening letter of the word Country's

parts.note: owned means had

explanation.surface: A national head once possessed territory on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Square dance for kids?

parts.note: not a country dance but a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares

explanation.definitionFit: Children hop and jump through a grid of chalked boxes in this playground game.

clue.text: Stop streetcar dropping engineers on street

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: Tennessee Williams's play A Streetcar Named Desire supplies the streetcar's name
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A tram stops letting off engineers on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes RE (Royal Engineers) from DESIRE, leaving DESI.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or refrain from an action is the same as to stop.

clue.text: Marriage partner facing one, possibly

parts.note: facing means opposite
one is an example of a number

explanation.surface: A spouse sits across from you, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart who matches you in another position, and a spouse is one's counterpart.

clue.text: Boundary through cover makes you furious

indicators.note: through means passing into the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lid is a cover
in cricket a boundary scores four runs, written in Roman numerals as IV

explanation.surface: A cricket shot to the boundary through the cover fielders enrages the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover is a fielding position and a boundary is a hit to the edge of the field; here a boundary is four runs, IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is a colloquial word for extremely angry.

clue.text: Darts throwers play with a skirl

definitions.meaning: tubes used to shoot darts by breath
a skirl is the shrill sound of bagpipes, so to sound bagpipes

explanation.definitionFit: Hunting tubes propel darts by breath; and a bagpiper is said to sound the instrument by breathing into the pipes.

clue.text: Our old coppers rained off before one

indicators.note: off means awry or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Old policemen were rained off ahead of one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Before decimalisation in 1971 British pennies, copper coins, were written d, from the Roman coin name.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman silver pieces gave the abbreviation d for British pre-decimal pennies, our former coppers.

clue.text: Selections of covered sweets, not cold inside

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken away
inside says the letter removed is from the interior of the word, not an end

parts.note: choc ices are ice creams covered in chocolate

explanation.surface: An assortment of chocolate-covered treats with no chill inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' and 'inside' together remove the inner C from CHOCICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Selections are picks or options taken from a range.

clue.text: Entertainingly, one twists cotton -it irons out

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone presses cotton, smoothing the fabric with an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who bends the body into extreme shapes to amuse an audience.

clue.text: Disreputable on riotous break

indicators.note: break means smash apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowdy holiday gets a bad name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well known for something bad is to be disreputable.

clue.text: Contrived incentives to admit debt

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: spurs are incentives or goads
an IOU is a written note of a debt

explanation.surface: Bonuses are designed to get someone to own up to owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false or fake, not genuine, is contrived.

clue.text: Helper in white turns out for most urgent house-call

indicators.note: turns out means is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse in white uniform makes an emergency home visit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament the House of Commons is 'the house'; a whip underlined three times is a party's most urgent order to attend and vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's strongest instruction calling its MPs to vote in the Commons, the most pressing summons to the chamber.

clue.text: Long cakes from city retreats

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
lairs are hideaways or retreats

explanation.surface: Finger pastries come from urban hideaways.
explanation.definitionFit: These are oblong choux pastries filled with cream.

clue.text: Popular field trip for a sceptic

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: trip means stumble, so these letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A doubter goes on a fashionable country outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonbeliever who rejects a religion, broadly someone doubting.

clue.text: Wells manuscript showing sudden bursts of emotion

parts.note: wells are mineral springs, also called spas

explanation.surface: An H. G. Wells manuscript reveals fits of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden fits or outbursts, of feeling as well as muscle.

clue.text: Country girl in Reading?

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A country girl is placed in the English town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the English town, capitalised to hide the sense of perusing a text.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful read through a text.

clue.text: Female beauty in America getting people in a state

parts.note: luster, the American spelling of lustre, means radiance or beauty

explanation.surface: An American beauty queen gets people into a flap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a nervous agitated state is being in a flap or tizzy.

clue.text: Trunk held in curator's office

indicators.note: held in says the answer is kept inside the following words

explanation.surface: A trunk is stored in the museum keeper's room.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs, is the torso.

clue.text: Sandpiper, we hear

parts.note: a sandpiper is a wader of beaches, and its piping call is what is heard by the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper is a wading bird found on beaches and coasts.

clue.text: Pack animal in endless tunnel

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a burrow is an animal's tunnel

explanation.surface: A packhorse is in an underground passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A burro is a small donkey used to carry loads.

clue.text: Southern wood for window frame

parts.note: ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Southern timber is used for the window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the frame holding the glass panes of a window.

clue.text: Wherein lots of people are knocked down

definitions.text: Wherein lots of people are knocked down

parts.words: Wherein lots of people are knocked down
parts.note: not a brawl but an auction room, where lots are knocked down by the auctioneer's hammer

explanation.definitionFit: In auction rooms items called lots are knocked down, that is sold, to bidders.
